65-029.r: Biomagnification (bio-amplification) → rising concentration of a toxic substance such as pesticides in organisms at successively higher levels of a food chain.

65-030.r: Selective herbicides kill weeds without harming crops (A true) because weeds and crops absorb herbicides at different rates (R true, explains A).

65-031.r: Orobanche → parasitic weed found mainly in tobacco fields (also tomato and potato); about 150 species.

65-032.r: Destructive Insects and Pests Act (DIPA) → 1914; stops entry of crop pests and diseases into India and their inter-state spread.

65-033.r: Local flora information → herbarium: collection of preserved plants, catalogued and arranged for study and identification.
65-033.t: Herbarium = dried plants; planetarium = stars; sanitarium = health resort.

65-034.r: ICAR Day → 16 July (ICAR founded 16 July 1929 as a society, on Royal Commission on Agriculture report); from 2023 called 'Foundation and Technology Day'.

65-035.r: Order: National Maritime Day (5 April) → World Health Day (7 April) → World Athletics Day (7 May) → World Red Cross Day (8 May).

65-036.r: 5 June → World Environment Day; 1 December → World AIDS Day; 5 September → Teachers' Day; 16 October → World Food Day.

65-037.r: Wrong pair: World Homeopathy Day is 10 April, not 12 March. Correct: Environment Day 5 June, Earth Day 22 April, Yoga Day 21 June.

65-038.r: World T.B. Day → March 24; World AIDS Day → December 1; Anti-Leprosy Day → last Sunday of January (31 January in 1999); Ozone Day → September 16.

65-039.r: World Ozone Day → 16 September (Montreal Protocol adopted 16 September 1987; declared by UN General Assembly in 1994).

65-040.r: International AIDS Conference, July 2004 → Bangkok (Thailand); World AIDS Day → 1 December every year.

65-043.r: Calendar order: Anti-Leprosy Day (last Sunday of January) → World TB Day (24 March) → World Alzheimer's Day (21 September) → World AIDS Day (1 December).

65-044.r: Both wrong: World Water Day is 22 March (not 22 April); World Leprosy Day is last Sunday of January (not 30 June). Book gives (b) and (c).
65-044.t: 22 April is Earth Day, not Water Day.

65-045.r: World Diabetes Day → 14 November every year.

65-046.r: Minority Rights Day → 18 December; World AIDS Day → 1 December; World Animal Day → 4 October; World Food Day → 16 October. Book gives no single answer (*).

65-047.r: Cuckoo → never builds a nest; Lizard → sheds its tail (regrows); Blue whale → largest living creature; Chimpanzee → most intelligent animal.

65-048.r: Tamil Nadu → launched State-Level Committee for Vulture Conservation (October 2022) to implement Action Plan for Vulture Conservation 2020-2025.

65-049.r: Ten captive-bred Asian giant tortoises (Manouria emys) → released December 2022 in Ntangki National Park, Nagaland.

65-050.r: Both endangered (IUCN Red List): gharial crocodile (Gavialis gangeticus) is critically endangered; Indian elephant is endangered.

65-051.r: Cheetah ('hunting leopard') → went extinct in India over 70 years ago; Project Cheetah (from 2022) brought them from Namibia, South Africa, Botswana to Kuno National Park.

65-052.r: Sixth mass extinction → caused by humans: over-use of natural resources, habitat loss and fragmentation, ecosystem destruction, pollution, climate change (five earlier in 500 million years).

65-053.r: Wrong pair: inbuilt time-keeping system – biomass; biomass = biological material from living organisms (mostly plants). Correct: gene splicing–genetic engineering, amniocentesis, biodegradation.

65-054.r: Diseases of inner body parts → diagnosed with an endoscope (flexible tube with light and camera, e.g. for digestive tract).

65-055.r: Endoscope → long thin tube with light source and video camera; not a telescope, camera or microscope → 'None of these'.

65-056.r: Computed Tomography (CT / CAT scan) → uses X-rays taken from many angles, combined by computer into cross-sectional images.
65-056.t: CT = X-rays; MRI = magnetic field + radio waves; ultrasound = sound waves.

65-057.r: Barium meal before stomach X-ray → barium is a good absorber of X-rays, so the stomach stands out in contrast (detects tumours, ulcers).

65-058.r: EEG → brain; ECG → heart; EOG → eyes (retina); EMG → muscle.
65-058.h: Encephalo = brain, Cardio = heart, Oculo = eye, Myo = muscle.

65-059.r: Brain diseases → diagnosed by E.E.G. (electroencephalograph), which records brain waves; first recorded by Hans Berger with electrodes.

65-062.r: Audiogram → ear; E.C.G. → heart; E.E.G. → brain; Mammogram → breast.

65-063.r: MRI → based on nuclear magnetic resonance; uses powerful magnetic field, radio frequency pulses and a computer to image organs and soft tissues.

65-064.r: MRI = Magnetic Resonance Imaging → uses magnetic field and radio-wave pulses to picture organs inside the body.

65-065.r: MRI uses magnetic field and radio waves; it uses NO ionizing radiation (X-rays, gamma rays) → 'more than one of the above' (e).
65-065.t: X-ray is used in CT scan, not MRI.

65-067.r: BMD (Bone Mineral Density) test → diagnosis of osteoporosis (bone loses mineral density, fracture risk rises); measures calcium and minerals in bone.

65-070.r: Lithotripsy → breaking stones in kidney, bladder or ureter with ultrasound shockwaves; pieces pass out in urine.

65-071.r: Electron beam therapy → radiation therapy for certain cancers (skin lymphoma); types: spot treatment and total skin electron beam therapy.

65-072.r: Tetraplegia (quadriplegia) → paralysis (total or partial) of both hands and both legs.

65-073.r: Nutrition, respiration and synthesis → three major aspects of metabolism (catabolism = breakdown for energy; anabolism = synthesis).

65-074.r: Artificial silk → rayon, a manufactured cellulose fibre regenerated from wood and agricultural products.
